correctness.rationale: For odd p, the positive-exponent quadratic Gauss sum gives the exact paired Fourier expression T_p(n)=(2/sqrt(p)) sum_{1<=j<= (p-1)/2} chi(j)(2cos(j*pi/p))^n times cos(nj*pi/p) if p=1 mod4 and sin otherwise. For p>=5 the j=1 coefficient is positive; cos(pi/p)-cos(2pi/p)>=6/p^2 bounds relative harmonic decay by exp(-6n/p^2). Nonzero leading cos/sin has magnitude >=1/p, so the tail ratio is strictly <1 for n>=1+floor((p^2/6)log(p(p-3)/2)). The p=3 sum has only one harmonic. For p=3 mod4 and p|n, k<->n-k cancels the integer binomial sum exactly. The 2p sign cycle contains (p,p,0) or (p-1,p-1,2), proving densities. An independent integer Pascal/Legendre check covered all odd primes p<=23 through N_p+2p. Infinite validity follows from the inequalities, not finite tests.
